description: Holds expense details records (defined in the EF Core model), linked to expense category, expense sub category.
business_purpose: Used to track and report expense details records, including amounts and quantities, for the Accounts & Finance area.
record_granularity: One row represents one expense detail.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier of the expense detail.

columns.name: ExpenseHeaderid
columns.description: Expense headerid of the expense detail.

columns.name: confirmed_amount
columns.description: Confirmed amount of the expense detail.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Date and time of the record.

columns.name: expense_categoryid
columns.description: Reference to the expense category linked to this expense detail.

columns.name: expense_sub_categoryid
columns.description: Reference to the expense sub category linked to this expense detail.

columns.name: remarks
columns.description: Free-text remarks for the expense detail.

relationships.description: Each expense detail references one expense category (expense category).
Each expense detail references one expense sub category (expense sub category).

business_rules: date is the preferred date column for period-based reporting.
Use confirmed_amount / amount for monetary or quantity totals.
Join to Expense Category, Expense Sub Category through the foreign key columns to resolve names.
ExpenseDetails is defined in the EF Core model but was not found in the connected database, so it may not be deployed there.
common_queries: Expense Details by expense sub category

known_issues: amount, confirmed_amount are stored as floating point, so sums can carry small rounding differences.
confirmed_amount is nullable; use COALESCE when summing or comparing.

query_notes: Do not generate SQL against ExpenseDetails: no table or view with this name exists in the connected database.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT id) when counting expense detail records; joins can duplicate rows.
Use SUM(confirmed_amount) for totals of confirmed amount.
To resolve names, join on: expense_categoryid = ExpenseCategory.id; expense_sub_categoryid = ExpenseSubCategory.id.
Defined in the EF Core model but not found in the connected database; confirm it has been migrated before relying on it.
